CanTp v1.3.1 - the parts of the release package that TempCtl needs, unmodified
  source: https://github.com/rgravesjr-code/can-tp-dll  (tag v1.3.1)
  file:   CanTp_v1.3.1_unencrypted.zip
  sha256: 416cb605f1a9f7ba0b05cc25e2536f22a6b06ac6ad9211280601dd9cfaa6b339
  date:   2026-09-15

What is vendored (and nothing else):
  cantp.h                      the header, one for every build
  cantp.dll, cantp.lib         Windows x64
  x86\cantp.dll, cantp.lib     Windows x86
  linux-x64\libcantp.so        NI Linux RT x86_64 (cRIO-904x/905x/906x)
  linux-arm64\libcantp.so      aarch64 Linux (Raspberry Pi)
  linux-armhf\libcantp.so      32-bit ARM Linux
  tools\dbc2tables.py          .dbc -> CanTp tables; run by tools\make_tempctl_dbc.py --tables
  tools\ecdflat.py             J1939Msg(V4) cluster <-> bytes and .ecd reader; tools\make_tempctl_dbc.py
                               --ecd builds dbc	empctl.ecd with it and reads the result back (TempCtl v4)
  LICENSE.txt                  MIT

CanTp's documentation, source, tests, test executables and examples are in the
CanTp release package itself (the same zip, or the GitHub release). They are
not duplicated here.

Dependency rule:
  TempCtl and TempSim call CanTp_Define, CanTp_DefineFlat (v1.2.0+), CanTp_PackSgl, CanTp_Unpack,
  CanTp_RxFeed and the small query functions only. All but CanTp_DefineFlat exist
  unchanged since CanTp v1.0.0; CanTp_DefineFlat (the flattened ECD cluster) was
  added in v1.2.0, so the MINIMUM CanTp version for TempCtl v4 is 1.2.0 and any
  later 1.x release is a drop-in replacement. A new CanTp release does NOT
  require a TempCtl release; re-vendor (and bump TempCtl) only when TempCtl
  starts using a newer CanTp function, or when a TempCtl release is being cut
  anyway and the newest CanTp should ride along.

Do not edit anything in this folder; update by copying the files above out of
a newer CanTp release package and rewriting this file.
